title: Check your understanding: Automating Repository Checks

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of automating repository checks?
options: A repository release gate can verify branch, clean status, commit identity and successful checks before a release step. It should fail closed and state which precondition failed rather than continue on assumptions.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: A repository release gate can verify branch, clean status, commit identity and successful checks before a release step. It should fail closed and state which precondition failed rather than continue on assumptions.
questions.explanation: A repository release gate can verify branch, clean status, commit identity and successful checks before a release step. It should fail closed and state which precondition failed rather than continue on assumptions.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git status --porcelain=v1` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with automating repository checks?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
